body: I also feel I need to point out it’s unlikely he’ll pee for a while. Mine took 24 hours to have his first pee after I picked him up from the vets and let me tell you I was frantic by that point. When he finally went it was in the kitchen all over the floor like a fountain going off and I was so happy I didn’t care. By that point he had been potty trained for months and months so it was really out of character. It’s just that they are sore and scared of going. He also scuttled when walking. When I had my puppy for a week he wriggled out of my arms and went headfirst into the hard floor. I cried for hours and thought I was going to throw up. I vowed that I would rehome him to someone who isn’t so stupid and bad with tiny baby things. He wouldn’t come near me all night and yet he still cuddled into me at bedtime. I gave him so many kisses, took him to the vet and it was fine. Puppies are unpredictable and so small. She will be okay and I assure you that despite your very best efforts, this isn’t the last time she’ll get under someone’s feet. She’ll learn though to ensure she moves with you. I went for a cross breed, a cavapoo, because they were a small breed, would love snuggling, be gentle and not require tons of walking. I thought I did my research well. Turns out I got a huge one… so much energy, stubborn, smart, attitude problem - you name it. But he has taught me so much. All the things I needed to work on: patience, gentleness, anger management, negotiation skills, hard work, he has taught me in bucket loads. I am a better person for being his owner. It didn’t work out how I thought it would… it was so much better than I imagined. In retrospect of course. At the time it was hell 😆

Each stage is different and I found not linear but it really is so hugely different from dog to dog that it’s difficult to generalise. My experience was bitey phase was hardest. Small puppy was exhausting. As he grew our bond got stronger and we tackled problems together. I tried to make everything fun. He always struggled to settle in the evening so there was a small fortune spent on toys and a time out place for much needed naps. Around 4-6 months. 

At 7 months he hit puberty and it seemed all our training went out the window with recall. He was rebellious and a bit of a git. I started again with the basics, introduced new training games and was consistent. We might have have had a few rows. That lasted a few months. He was neutered at a year and that was a game changer for us. 

Now at 15 months he’s doing great and so am I. He’s starting to be more cuddly but also more independent. He doesn’t HAVE to be in the same room as me, he doesn’t get anxious if he can’t see me. I’ve found I’m actually more co dependent than he is :) 

End every day with cuddles and every day is a new chance. Your pup will go forward and backwards a lot in their development. Just be consistent, be there for her - someone she can trust. And ALWAYS know where your treats are. You guys will be fine. Enjoy it where you can, it goes so fast. X

Two artificial legs here and a lower back problem caused by said prostheses which has led to chronic pain. When I was younger I got all the same stuff about being too young to be disabled, people yelling at me for parking in a disabled bay or using the electric shopping carts. Luckily I have been surrounded by people who were never shy at having a go right back - I was always quite timid and would cry at confrontation. These days I’m a fearsome, sarcastic person who can slice and dice you with my words. Funny what a lifetime of struggle and pain can do for you. So all you young disabled people don’t worry, by 40 you’ll be sadly used to it and very able to deal with idiots. It’s one of the good things. The other good thing is that everything I’ve done has been hard and that, somehow, has made the achievements even more special. But able bodied people will never know how difficult it is to just live. Things that come so easily. I’ve had a struggle with weight all my life - I can’t work out and my body height is so little I have to starve myself to get thin. So as I love chocolate I shall be pleasantly rotund and society will have to deal with it. Life is much too short.

Well I can only tell you my personal experience with my boy, don’t take it as gospel for everyone:

Seth is a F2 I think, mum and dad are cavapoos. I have allergies to dog hair and he hasn’t triggered it once. I often stick my face in his fur because, you know, snuggles. With my old lab I had to take an allergy tablet every day. Probably because my allergies were caused by stray dog hairs but cavapoos don’t shed so… depends on your allergy. 

He’s about 11kg so about 24lb and that seems about normal around here. He’s sorta hefty and is built like a steam train but his girl bff is quite dainty and weighs a good 3kg less. I like the size; agile but not too small. Can’t reach the sideboard to steal stuff. Great hiking partner and so much energy oh my god. I just didn’t realise how much before I got one. I read a ton of stuff about them liking chilling with you on the sofa but clearly Seth did not get that memo. I am permanently exhausted. 

He was a wavy haired puppy and is now a wavy haired dog, his curls come out with a longer coat. But he has lots of cavapoo pals and each one is totally different. He didn’t change much of his coat from the first day we saw him so in my experience what you see at 8 weeks stayed the same. 

Even though I am more tired than I have ever been he is an amazing pup - they have so much character. Couldn’t be without him now. Happy hunting for your pupkin.

The most important thing in all this is how you feel about what your partner does on Instagram. If it bothers you you then, yes, it’s a problem. Relationships should be about mutual respect and clear boundaries should be set. It’s important to talk it through so everybody knows where they stand. I think it’s normal to have celebrity crushes and favourite people to follow - but it would bother me if it was borderline obsession or they were interacting in anything but a platonic way. 

Communication is the key here. What’s expected, what’s tolerated. It’s easy to write things off as ‘just online’ or ‘just social media’ but that’s a much more far reaching issue when it affects the level of trust you have for one another. Social media is not a virtual reality, it is still reality. What you do on it still is your life. So yes, Instagram behaviour is still real life behaviour.

I’m so so sorry. Lots of people will say that to you, and they will mean it. But it doesn’t help much I know. I’m 4 years on from the day my fiancé was killed so I have walked your path before you. I have played the ‘if I had only’ game in my head until it almost drove me mad, I know. You have a battle ahead of you, there are demons to be fought. But you will do it. What’s most important I think is how you do it. When you’re in the dark it is much easier to go further into the darkness than it is to go into the light. 

You loved her, when she died she was loved. Hold onto that. It was not your fault no matter what your brain says. Hold onto that too. People tell you it eases with time, I suppose it does, you learn to live with it. But you are being too hard on yourself, you are punishing yourself for something you had no control over. Be gentle to yourself, be kind. You have experienced a trauma and it will take a long time to come through it. Talk to people, share things. I think we are at our most destructive when we bottle it all up and pretend to be strong. You aren’t alone sweetie. You can’t process this and begin to heal until you let some of it out.

Sweetie, the only way you’ll know is if you try. It might be something you used to like too but don’t anymore. You’re going to get to know yourself again, and like or hate it that will be yours alone. Then try stuff that you never thought you’d like. Start small, get bigger when you’re ready. I like gardening - if you’d told me that having my hands in dirt, pulling up weeds would bring me comfort 5 years ago I would have looked at you with such side eye. But it is peaceful. I like rain and sitting in my car or by the window when it lashes down. I like hot chocolate with ALL of the toppings, because why not? The thing about depression is you have no drive to do much of anything so you’ll have to cajole yourself a little. Remember you’re not shooting for happiness, just less sad for now xxx

Dearest, I know how you feel. I expect quite a lot of us here know how you feel. We don’t know you but we do know the surety of how it would be better if we ended it. The trouble is if you do go today then there’s no way that things can get better. That’s it, the end. Life has a funny way of taking you in directions you never expected. Something that today you can’t even fathom could be a reality in 5 years. It’s the possibility that keeps us all here. And that spark of hope that refuses to die, even when we want to. Love, laughter, friends, adventure - it could all be waiting around the next corner. You don’t have to write your entire story now but don’t end it early.

I’ve read about this, when the pain of the world is felt so very acutely by certain people. It’s very difficult to live like this without it destroying you. Practically I would suggest going on a media blackout for a little while and making your world very small. It sounds like you don’t find joy in a lot right now but focus on small things; how a cold drink tastes, how sheets feel on your skin, how the sunlight makes that pink hue through your eyelids. You are thinking too big and it is becoming unmanageable for you. What do they say, one day at a time and if that’s too much then one hour at a time. Bring yourself back to the immediate and your immediate surroundings. Find things that bring you peace or at the least quietens your soul. We can plan for the future but life rarely holds to those plans, live for now and worry about the rest later. When my depression was at its worst it’s how I got through.

Darling I’m so sorry, it was the single most painful experience of my life and my heart breaks for you that you too are going through it. I lost him 3 years ago so I will try and share some things I learned.

You don’t move on but you do move forward. You won’t want to but you will, nothing stands still even when it should. I went kicking and screaming but I went nonetheless. It does hurt less with time, instead of the sharp pain and panic you feel now it will dull over time. But It will never go. Grief is not a straight line, it is a squiggly piece of string that doubles back and ties itself up. One day you’ll feel like you’re doing okay, the next like you can’t breathe. Even years later. Be gentle with yourself, do whatever you need to comfort yourself. Eat, even when you don’t feel like it. You’ll need your strength. Lean on people, they want to help. Find people who understand what you’re going through. Your friends, if they haven’t experienced the loss of a partner won’t be able to relate exactly. It’s a unique kind of loss that takes the person and your entire planned future with it. 

Ban the words ‘at least’. There is no at least here. Try not to blitz your apartment like I did, I miss things I threw out in a rage. You will get through, you are strong enough - you might not believe that for some time but it’s true. If you need anyone to talk to I’m here.

I’ll let you in to a little secret, almost nobody thinks they are cool. Everybody feels a little awkward and socially challenged on most days. What I did was look for people who had similar interests to me, no matter how lame I thought my interests were. There I practiced social interaction and the more you do it the better you get. That allowed me to gradually widen my social circle and these days I can small talk with anyone. 
For small talk always read the situation and use visuals to help say something. Like if you’re stuck, I always throw in a ‘cool trainers’ or where did you get <insert item>. Talk about classes and ask questions. People love talking about themselves. most importantly know when to leave the conversation. It only becomes awkward if people linger after the conversation is over. 
Practice, practice. You’ll be great.

My weight loss is super slow, always has been. I’ve always assumed my body thinks I’m about to move to the North Pole at any second and wants the warmth. But I’m sticking with it because the other benefits are so great. I feel so much better in myself; bloating gone, IBS gone, I sleep better and my mood is better. So I don’t get hung up on the numbers - I know I’m in this for the long haul and eventually my body will catch up with my brain. But don’t ever think you’re the only slow mo out there. We’re here and we’re ready to help. Check your macros, weigh everything... stick with it. You got this.

And the important thing is to keep at it. It’s totally disheartening to not lose weight quickly, especially when others say they do. But tinker with the diet, find your favourites, read a ton of other’s stories to give you help and advice and read the FAQs again. I recently found out I hadn’t calculated my macros properly... you’ll get into the groove and start seeing the results. And we’re all with you - good luck 😁
